name: 7-keto DHEA
short: In the cited sources, a 4-week study in 22 healthy men found no difference from placebo in adverse experiences or laboratory values; a review of 4 studies reported no serious adverse effects.
text: In the cited sources, human safety data on 7-keto DHEA come from small, short studies. In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in 22 healthy men given the acetylated form (3-acetyl-7-oxo-DHEA) in escalating doses up to 200 mg/day for 4 weeks, there were no differences between the treatment and placebo groups in clinical laboratory values or reported minor adverse experiences, and blood hormone concentrations (the study measured testosterone, estradiol, cortisol, thyroxin and insulin) were in general unaffected and stayed within the normal range. A systematic review of 7-keto DHEA for body weight included four studies in which no serious adverse effects were reported, and its authors concluded that further studies are needed to clarify safety. The placebo-controlled safety study was limited to healthy men and 4 weeks of use. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
